headline: Bare-Metal Cloud Computers Built Specifically for AI Agents
lede: Agent Computer is a new infrastructure service that provisions isolated cloud machines tailored for autonomous AI agents rather than human developers. Where most cloud providers sell general-purpose virtual machines, Agent Computer is designed around the workflows agents actually need: fast file I/O, browser access out of the box, and programmable port publishing for webhooks. The tweet is a straightforward product announcement from one of its builders.
body:
The service runs on *Firecracker*, the open-source microVM technology originally developed at Amazon Web Services. Firecracker is notable for booting Linux workloads in under 125 milliseconds with a minimal attack surface — properties that matter when an orchestration layer needs to spin up and tear down machines at the cadence of agent tasks rather than human deployments. Agent Computer layers its own provisioning logic, called `computer-host`, on top of Firecracker and runs directly on bare metal, cutting out the extra virtualisation hop that typical cloud tenants accept.

Storage and network figures are concrete: **~3 GB/s file transfer** over NVMe and up to 1.2 Gb/s upload over shared NAT. Those numbers matter for agents that pull large model weights, cache datasets, or stream results back to an orchestrator. Compute is configurable between 2 GiB and 64 GiB of RAM, with storage up to 250 GiB, subject to available host capacity — the caveat signals that the platform is still capacity-constrained rather than elastically overprovisioned like a hyperscaler.

Every machine boots from a standard *guest image* that arrives pre-configured with browser access, SSH, and port publishing primitives. Port publishing is public by default — suited for agents that need to expose webhooks or test an app endpoint without manual networking — though a `--private` flag gates the URL behind an authenticated session. A macOS variant is available via QEMU/KVM, though Linux-exclusive features such as exec, file operations, and snapshots are not yet ported to it.

The business model is *usage-based*: runtime CPU and RAM, hot storage, and cold storage are billed as separate line items. That granularity rewards short-lived agent runs and penalises idle machines, which aligns incentives reasonably well for the workload. The CLI, TypeScript SDK, and REST API give three different surfaces for integration, which is table stakes for infrastructure targeting developers building automated pipelines.

concepts.definition: An open-source virtualisation technology developed at AWS that runs lightweight Linux virtual machines — called microVMs — with very fast boot times and a minimal attack surface. It underpins AWS Lambda and AWS Fargate. Because each microVM is strongly isolated, it suits multi-tenant environments where many separate workloads must run side by side safely.

Running software directly on physical server hardware without a host operating system or hypervisor in between. This eliminates one layer of virtualisation overhead, delivering closer-to-hardware CPU and I/O performance. The tradeoff is reduced flexibility in provisioning: a bare-metal tenant occupies a machine fully rather than sharing it as a thin slice.

Exposing a specific network port on a private machine to the public internet via a stable URL. In Agent Computer's model, a published port is reachable without an active session, making it suitable for webhooks — callbacks from external services that expect a persistent, addressable endpoint. Adding a privacy flag restricts access to authenticated sessions instead.

Non-Volatile Memory Express, a storage protocol designed for solid-state drives connected directly to a CPU over PCIe lanes. It is significantly faster than older protocols like SATA or SAS. The ~3 GB/s figure Agent Computer cites is typical of high-end NVMe in a data-centre context, compared with roughly 500 MB/s for a commodity cloud block-storage volume.
